what.text: This page follows refugees from the Central African Republic living in Cameroon.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 277873 Central African refugees in Cameroon, 41.2% of all Central African refugees and more than in any other host country.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Chad host the next largest numbers.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of the Central African Republic in several periods since 2001.
From 2009 to 2014 the groups fighting the government include the CPJP, Seleka and anti-Balaka; from 2017 to 2025 they include anti-Balaka, the UPC and the CPC.

when.text: The main years of displacement in the data are 2014 to 2025, after a big change between 2013 and 2014.
UNHCR's figure for Cameroon rose from 15000 in 1982 to a peak of 353956 in 2023.
Returns from Cameroon to the Central African Republic were highest in 2018 in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees in Cameroon only.
People displaced inside the Central African Republic are counted separately by UNHCR and by IDMC, and their figures are never added.
The sources don't say which routes people took or where in Cameroon they live.
